sections.overview: The V-Moth is a geometrid whose British populations are often found around cultivated fruit bushes.
sections.identification: UKMoths gives an adult wingspan of 25–30 mm.
sections.habitat: It favours gardens, allotments and other cultivated places where currants or gooseberries grow.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on several currants and gooseberries in the genus Ribes.
sections.behavior: In central Europe, adults mainly fly in June and July, rarely in late May or early August.
sections.reproduction: The egg overwinters, and caterpillars are usually found from mid-April to early June.
sections.ecology: Unlike the conifer-feeding Macaria liturata and Macaria signaria, its caterpillars use Ribes shrubs, often grown in gardens.
sections.conservation: UKMoths reports that it appears to be declining in Britain, although it remains widely distributed there.
